_what: Experimentally supported aggregation-critical regions. The validation set.
_why: A benchmark of aggregation predictors is only as sound as the ground truth it scores against. Nothing in this project is sounder than this table, so it carries provenance per row rather than per file.

_numbering.TRIOBP-1: 652-residue frame of NP_008963.3 (UniProt Q9H2D6-7). Papers using the older 593-residue frame need 59 ADDED. One paper gives the shorter variant as 593 in one place and 597 in another. A table that mixes frames without normalising is silently wrong by 59 residues.

_columns.construct: WHICH CONSTRUCT established it. A region can be necessary in one construct and dispensable in another; both results can be correct. Without this column the benchmark scores against a moving target.
_columns.found_by: how the region was discovered. 'prediction' rows are CIRCULAR for a predictor benchmark and must be analysed separately.
_columns.verified_against_publisher_pdf: false means nobody has opened the source and checked this row.

regions.evidence: truncation series in SH-SY5Y cells, insolubility fractionation, blinded counts
regions.construct: truncated construct already lacking both the optional N-terminus and the PH domain, so the central linker was the only aggregation route left
regions.found_by: experimental scanning; the authors state explicitly it was NOT predicted
regions.note: USE THIS AS THE GROUND TRUTH for TRIOBP-1 -- the whole 25-residue linker -- with 324-328 and 333-340 recorded below as assay-specific sub-annotations rather than competing boundary claims.
regions.sequence_provenance: DERIVED, NOT READ. The source paper prints this sequence only in Figure 12B. It was reconstructed from the C-terminal 652 residues of UniProt Q9H2D6 and passes three independent consistency checks: the proline and charge composition matches the paper's description, genuine coiled-coil heptads appear at the stated CC1/CC2 flanks, and the 593-frame offset reproduces the identical string. VERIFY AGAINST FIGURE 12B before any published use -- the gatekeeper result depends on it.

regions.evidence: N-terminal deletions identified these as essential
regions.found_by: experimental, truncating from the N-terminal end

regions.evidence: fragments starting at 324 or 333 aggregated, at 349 did not; 341 and 343 partial
regions.found_by: experimental narrowing, truncating from the C-terminal end
regions.note: THE DECISIVE TEST SITS HERE. This 8-mer is 0% gatekeeper residues -- indistinguishable from VQIVYK or GNNQQNY on that measure -- while the 25-mer containing it is 48%. If this scores POSITIVE on a hexapeptide-trained predictor in isolation, the prediction failure is about FLANKING CONTEXT, which is a different and arguably better paper than intrinsic core chemistry. Compute it before framing anything.

regions.evidence: deletion reduced aggregation; deleting 1-59 together with 333-340 nearly abolished it
regions.construct: FULL-LENGTH protein, where a second aggregation route survives
regions.found_by: tested after an unexpected result, not from prediction
regions.note: this row and 324-348 look contradictory and are not: two putative aggregation domains, removing either alone leaves some aggregation, removing both abolishes it.

regions.evidence: stable dimer by size-exclusion chromatography and circular dichroism
regions.found_by: earlier bioinformatics pointed here; the deletion work did NOT support it
regions.note: NEGATIVE-CONTROL ROW: prediction pointed here and experiment did not confirm it. Keep it; a benchmark needs its false positives.

regions.evidence: ITC, DLS, CD, negative-stain EM, solid-state NMR on recombinant protein
regions.construct: isolated C-region, E. coli, tagged, up to 400 uM, sonicated, two weeks
regions.found_by: boundaries from ESPRIT, an experimental screen
regions.note: The paper's own framing is that it does not establish whether DISC1 aggregates in vivo. Contains three free cysteines (C698, C762, C782) and no study reports a reducing agent.

regions.evidence: solid-state NMR beta-strand chemical shifts, EM morphology
regions.found_by: RADAR sequence-repeat search; standard amyloid predictors failed
regions.CAUTION_2026_11_15: THIS IS A DOCKING RESTRAINT, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Nothing was deposited -- no coordinates, no chemical shifts, no EM map, no accession, and the paper has no data-availability section. The EM was negative-stain TEM at 120 kV with no resolution reported, and the model is a MODELLER protomer built with ANTIPARALLEL BETA-STRAND RESTRAINTS IMPOSED AS INPUT (segments 716-737 and 739-761) then docked into that envelope. Re-modelling it would re-assert the input, not confirm the topology. The paper also states its own boundary two ways, 716-761 and 717-761. The 2025 follow-up states verbatim 'No data was used for the research described in the article'.
regions.found_by_note: RADAR is a sequence method, so this row is partly circular for a sequence-predictor benchmark and must be analysed separately.

regions.evidence: sequence repeat, consistent with ssNMR shifts
regions.note: the restraint segments used to build the model above; not independent of it

regions.evidence: the delta-22 splice deletion, named for its 22 residues
regions.note: Overlaps the reported core at 748-761 (fourteen residues); 762-769 falls outside it. So it removes PART of the core, not all of it, and the Abstract's wording is imprecise. The authors report delta-22 point mutants T754S and P758R abolishing binding to Dixdc1, LIS1 and PCM1, so this segment carries a protein-interaction surface as well as fibril propensity.

regions.evidence: truncation and deletion in cells; no single D, I, S or C region aggregates alone
regions.note: ADDED 15 Nov 2026. A ~32-residue linker C-terminal of the D region, outside all four structured domains. CONTRADICTS the C-terminal in vitro result above, and both groups acknowledge the conflict. It is also the second case of the central pattern: an inter-domain linker in a coiled-coil scaffold protein, missed by every predictor. Caveat: same lab as the TRIOBP-1 work, so this is a second case rather than independent replication.

_rows_deliberately_excluded.DISC1 L607F: DO NOT ADD. It appears in neither Cukkemane paper. The 2025 paper discusses L807-FS, a frameshift downstream of residue 807 -- a different residue and a different lesion. L607F's characterised phenotype is disrupted nuclear targeting and reduced ATF4 interaction, with no aggregation structure behind it.
_rows_deliberately_excluded.DISC1 S704C: Not an aggregation region. Measured from PDB 9RUX coordinates: its mouse equivalent is buried behind 96 heavy-atom neighbours with no cysteine sulfur within 11.76 A in any of four chains. A folding and packing variant.

_the_target_count: The plan sets a floor of roughly fifteen well-evidenced rows before proceeding. This file holds ten, of which several are sub-annotations or circular. Widening to every protein with fragment-level aggregation mapping -- not only the psychiatric ones -- is the outstanding task.
_the_inventory: A 146-row inventory across ~45 proteins now exists at research_notes/Mental illness aggregation structures/aggregation_region_ground_truth_inventory.md. About 20 rows are circular and about 40 are independent across ~25 proteins -- roughly five times this file. That answers the statistical-power problem. Rows must be read and verified before migrating them here.
_CPAD_CONTAMINATION_WARNING: DO NOT BULK-IMPORT FROM CPAD. The CANYA paper (Thompson 2025, Sci Adv, PMC12042874) states verbatim that "several of these methods (including TANGO, CamSol, and Aggrescan) were directly trained on sequences within CPAD", which violates out-of-sample evaluation on those datasets. Drawing rows from CPAD without per-row provenance checks reproduces exactly the violation that paper names. The same paper reports that on WALTZ-DB hexapeptides "no method significantly outperformed hydrophobicity".
_circularity_cannot_be_grepped: The predictor-provenance column cannot be filled by keyword search. Circularity is PROTEIN-specific, not lab- or journal-specific: the same laboratory in the same era produced rows of opposite status, and so did two segments of one protein. Four rows would be wrongly flagged by a grep, because a post-hoc remark about a predictor, or the use of a disorder or helix-propensity tool, is not prediction-guided discovery. Each row has to be read.
_frame_traps_are_worse_than_assumed: Beyond the TRIOBP-1 59-residue offset: hnRNPA1's two frames differ by an INTERNAL ALTERNATIVE EXON, so one commonly cited range exists only in the minor-isoform frame and converting it by a constant offset yields a sequence that does not occur. Tau's canonical accession is 758-residue big tau while the entire literature uses the 441-residue frame. Huntingtin's frame shifts with the repeat length.
_COAGGREGATION_IS_THREE_DIFFERENT_PHENOM: ADDED 15 Nov 2026. The word 'co-aggregation' names at least THREE unrelated things, and all three surface in searches this project runs. (1) PROTEIN hetero-aggregation -- two misfolded proteins forming mixed oligomers or fibrils. This is the only sense this project means. (2) EPIDEMIOLOGICAL / FAMILIAL co-aggregation -- diagnoses clustering in families. Liu F-C et al., Clin Epidemiol 10:631-641 (2018) is titled 'Familial aggregation of Parkinson's disease and COAGGREGATION WITH NEUROPSYCHIATRIC DISEASES' and reports raised SCHIZOPHRENIA risk in first-degree relatives of PD patients. Any query pairing 'coaggregation' with 'schizophrenia' will return this literature, which is population genetics and says nothing about protein structure. See also Feldman et al., Eur J Epidemiol 29:49-56 (2014), 'modest familial co-aggregation between dementia and parkinsonism'. (3) BACTERIAL coaggregation -- specific adhesion between genetically distinct bacterial cells in biofilms, mediated by lectin-saccharide interactions. Nothing to do with amyloid. As of 15 Nov 2026 this repository is clean of senses (2) and (3); keep it that way, and label the sense whenever the word is used.
